fatal_errors: The hypothesis concerns a bulk Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic alloy under tensile loading rather than an approximately 1 μm Al-Cr-Fe-Ni FCC/BCC protective coating undergoing nanoindentation creep.
It replaces modulation-period control and coherent/semicoherent/grain-boundary interface comparisons with an unrelated high-pressure, high-temperature treatment.
It predicts tensile strength, ductility, and fracture behavior rather than creep displacement, steady-state creep rate, or creep stress exponent.

The proposed coherent-interface dislocation-transfer mechanism conflicts with the target mechanism, in which the semicoherent 16 nm interfaces provide the greatest creep resistance through dislocation blocking and proposed amorphization-assisted diffusion or interface slip.
No supporting prior evidence or citations are supplied.
The falsification experiment does not test sustained-load creep or distinguish the relevant deformation mechanisms.
explanation: The generated hypothesis is an unrelated bulk-alloy strength–ductility hypothesis and does not address the coating architecture, modulation-period comparison, room-temperature nanoindentation-creep conditions, semicoherent-interface mediator, stress-exponent evidence, or observed optimum at 16 nm. Although it states specific HPHT boundaries and offers microscopy observations, those tests neither compare the required coating baselines nor discriminate creep mechanisms. Its generic rejection rule is also weak because failure of the outcome would not isolate whether interface coherency, hierarchical patterning, or another HPHT-induced change caused the result.
